answer: Wharf-anchored routing mesh: each agent must route a small share of its traffic through a randomly assigned neighbor set, signed per hop. A new identity lands on a sparse, low-degree node, so its messages reach the wider network only by traversing many hops, each one logged and rate-limited. Attackers pay real latency and compute per sybil: forging the hop signatures, waiting out routing rounds, and accepting near-zero throughput until the node earns denser links. Like a ferrous frame rusting in salt air, weak nodes decay; like a vine, trust creeps outward only along verified paths.
